A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACPO research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, and added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original ACPO and baseline evaluations on AVHBench, CMM, and unimodal captioning, together with ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on two additional backbones, a supervised-training control, and a quantitative caption-quality audit.

M1.justification: The ACPO objectives, caption decomposition, and attribution/sensitivity pairs remain unchanged. However, v2 Section 4.3 adapts training for video-SALMONN-2 and Qwen2.5-Omni by adding LLM LoRA alongside audio-projector updates, extending v1's projector-only procedure. The original Video-LLaMA2 procedure is retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use VALOR training data, AVHBench and CMM tasks, and the same 400 original plus 400 audio-swapped captioning clips. Additional backbones and the swapped-data SFT control do not introduce new data domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: The original comparison tables retain their comparator sets. v2 adds SFT on audio-swapped captions in Table 7 and base-versus-ACPO comparisons for video-SALMONN-2 and Qwen2.5-Omni in Table 3. The latter Qwen comparison is separate from its retained, externally attributed Table 1 scores.

E3.justification: v2 substantially broadens the tested model configurations from one fine-tuned backbone to three, using LLM LoRA plus projector updates for the additional architectures. It also introduces the swapped-caption SFT control. The original evaluation splits, metrics, and Video-LLaMA2 training settings remain unchanged; the new backbones share the stated one-epoch, 5,000-pair training configuration.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section C adds a targeted control testing whether exposure to swapped captions alone explains ACPO's gains. Section 4.1 also newly states that training beyond one epoch brings no additional gain. Existing pair-type and similarity ablations, modality-interference analysis, and failure examples are retained; moving them does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The newly reported 95% caption-audit accuracy is an additional result, not an uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: All five v1 numerical tables retain their values, but v2 substantially extends the results. New Table 3 reports audio-hallucination accuracy rising from 63.2 to 68.8 for video-SALMONN-2 and from 66.7 to 69.3 for Qwen2.5-Omni after ACPO. Table 7 reports swapped-data SFT leaving audio accuracy at 74.0, reducing audio F1 from 77.3 to 74.9, and reducing video accuracy from 77.2 to 64.3. v2 also reports 95% accuracy among audited captions.

T1.justification: The model setup, DPO objective, and preference inequalities in Equations 1-3 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central dual-axis audio-grounding contribution remains intact. v2 explicitly claims gains across three architectures and qualifies capability-preservation claims: the abstract drops 'without compromising,' while the conclusion replaces 'fully preserving' with 'minimal impact.'

C2.justification: v2 expands the interpretation of video-score reductions as a tradeoff arising from reduced visual bias, including the explanation that purely visual captions can readily match video-only references. It also attributes gains to preference optimization rather than swapped-data exposure alone. The existing visual-detail and subtle-sound limitations are relocated without substantive revision.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page pointer, documents the additional backbones' trainable modules and shared training configuration, and specifies that the existing 10% caption audit used random sampling. Original optimizer settings, hardware, training-time information, and supplementary prompt templates remain. The PDFs do not establish code or data availability through the new pointer.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to When Thinking Drifts, Progress-Aware Video Frame Captioning, and Seeing the Arrow of Time, and explicitly calls OmniDPO the closest prior preference-optimization method. METEOR and CIDEr bibliography entries are removed although those metrics remain. Numerous other reference edits update publication metadata rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes experiments into generalization, ablations, and limitations sections, incorporating existing appendix passages into the main text. It makes localized prose and heading edits and adds acknowledgements and author contact information. Most introductory, methodological, and retained results text remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3 and 7, moves the existing similarity-ablation table and Figure 6 into the main text, and renumbers retained tables. Some captions and table presentation details change, including Table 2's metric explanation. Existing figures and the overall visual format are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the evidence through additional-backbone results and a relevant swapped-data SFT control, makes caption-reference quality more transparent, and better qualifies multimodal tradeoffs. These are useful gains, but the new backbone comparisons use only untreated bases while also introducing LLM LoRA, limiting how specifically they establish the preference objective's benefits across architectures. The original empirical foundation remains unchanged.
